title: npm & package.json
subtitle: Package management — installing dependencies, scripts, semver, and lock files
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Installing, versioning, and sharing third-party code manually is error-prone. Projects need a repeatable way to declare their dependencies.
whyItExists.solution: npm (Node Package Manager) is the default package manager. package.json declares what your project is and what it depends on. npm install reads it and downloads exact dependencies. The lock file (package-lock.json) pins exact versions for reproducible builds.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Every Node.js project. npm is bundled with Node.js. Alternatives: pnpm (faster, disk-efficient) and yarn (older alternative).
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: N/A — every Node project needs a package manager.

explainModes.beginner: npm is like an app store for code. `npm install express` downloads the Express library and saves it in node_modules. package.json is a config file that lists your project's info and all its dependencies. Running `npm install` in a new clone of your project re-installs everything listed there.
explainModes.simple: Key commands: npm init -y (create package.json), npm install package (save to dependencies), npm install -D package (save to devDependencies), npm uninstall package, npm run script-name. package.json fields: name, version, main, scripts, dependencies, devDependencies, engines. Semver: ^1.2.3 (compatible — any 1.x.x), ~1.2.3 (patch only — 1.2.x), 1.2.3 (exact). package-lock.json: never edit manually; commit it.
explainModes.standard: Scripts: npm scripts run shell commands — build, test, start, dev are conventions. Scripts can reference node_modules/.bin executables without full path. npx: run an npm package binary without installing globally. node_modules: never commit it (.gitignore). dependencies vs devDependencies: runtime deps go in dependencies (express, prisma); build tools and test frameworks go in devDependencies (vite, jest, typescript, eslint). In production, `npm install --omit=dev` skips devDependencies.
explainModes.technical: package.json 'exports' field: controls what files of your package are importable (replaces 'main'). Supports conditional exports: '.' can export different files for CJS vs ESM. 'workspaces': monorepo support — multiple packages in one repo. npm scripts lifecycle: pre and post hooks — pretest runs before test, postinstall runs after install. npm link: symlink a local package for development. peer dependencies: packages that the user must install (e.g., react is a peerDependency of react-dom).
explainModes.deepDive: Semver resolution: npm uses a range resolver. ^1.2.3 allows >=1.2.3 <2.0.0 (major locked). ~1.2.3 allows >=1.2.3 <1.3.0 (minor locked). 0.x.y is special — ^0.2.3 allows >=0.2.3 <0.3.0 (no compatible guarantee before 1.0.0). Lock file: package-lock.json stores exact resolved versions, checksums, and the full dependency tree. This ensures identical installs across machines and CI. npm ci: installs from lock file only (faster, no resolution, fails if lock and package.json disagree — ideal for CI). npm audit: scans for known vulnerabilities in your dependency tree.

content.code:
{
  "name": "my-api",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "A simple REST API",
  "main": "src/index.js",
  "type": "module",
  "engines": { "node": ">=20.0.0" },

  "scripts": {
    "start":   "node src/index.js",
    "dev":     "node --watch src/index.js",
    "build":   "tsc",
    "test":    "node --test",
    "lint":    "eslint src/",
    "format":  "prettier --write src/"
  },

  "dependencies": {
    "express":    "^4.18.2",
    "dotenv":     "^16.3.1",
    "zod":        "^3.22.4"
  },

  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/node":    "^20.0.0",
    "typescript":     "^5.3.3",
    "eslint":         "^8.56.0",
    "prettier":       "^3.1.1"
  }
}

# Initialize a new project
npm init -y                  # creates package.json with defaults

# Install packages
npm install express          # save to 'dependencies'
npm install -D typescript    # save to 'devDependencies'
npm install -g nodemon       # global install (available everywhere)
npx create-vite my-app       # run without installing

# Manage packages
npm uninstall lodash         # remove and update package.json
npm update                   # update all to latest within semver range
npm outdated                 # show which packages have newer versions

# Run scripts (from package.json "scripts")
npm start                    # shorthand for npm run start
npm test                     # shorthand for npm run test
npm run dev                  # custom scripts need 'run'
npm run build

# Info
npm list                     # show installed packages
npm audit                    # check for security vulnerabilities
npm ci                       # clean install from lock file (CI environments)

questions.question: What is the difference between `dependencies` and `devDependencies`?
options: dependencies are required at runtime (production); devDependencies are only needed during development (build tools, test frameworks, linters)
dependencies are always installed globally; devDependencies are local
There is no practical difference — the split is only for documentation
questions.explanation: dependencies (express, dotenv) are needed when your app runs. devDependencies (typescript, jest, eslint, prettier) are tools you need to develop the app but not to run it. In production CI/CD, you run `npm install --omit=dev` (or `--production`) to skip devDependencies — smaller deploy, faster install, smaller attack surface.

faq.a: Never commit node_modules — add it to .gitignore. It can contain thousands of files and hundreds of MB. Instead commit package.json and package-lock.json. Anyone cloning your repo runs `npm install` to restore node_modules. The lock file ensures they get the exact same versions you used.

npm run build && npm start — build then start in production
